x: Kalpakkam (Chennai, Tamil Nadu) is known for its nuclear plants and affiliated research installations. Madras Atomic Power Station (MAPS) is a comprehensive nuclear power production, fuel reprocessing, and waste treatment facility that includes plutonium fuel fabrication for fast breeder reactors (FBRs). x: India signed a comprehensive safeguards agreement (CSA) with the IAEA in 2009 and also subscribed to more scrutiny by the body, entering into an "Additional Protocol" for the Application of Safeguards to Civilian Nuclear Facilities in 2014. It International Relations PMF IAS Misc – 86 notably strengthens the IAEA's capacity to ensure the peaceful utilisation of all nuclear materials within nations having comprehensive safeguards agreements. s: In India, why are some nuclear reactors kept under "IAEA Safeguards" while others are not?
o: Some use Uranium and others use thorium.
Some use imported uranium and others use domestic supplies.
Some are operated by foreign enterprises and others are operated by domestic enterprises.
Some are Stateowned and others are privately-owned.
x: Nuclear reactors using imported uranium are often placed under International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards to ensure the nuclear material is used exclusively for peaceful purposes and not for military applications. In contrast, reactors that utilise domestic uranium may not be subject to the same level of international oversight. This step was taken by India in 2014 to demonstrate that its nuclear energy programme was for peaceful purposes. This is a necessary step under the Indo- US nuclear deal. India procures nuclear fuel through spot deals with several countries, including Kazakhstan, Russia, France, Uzbekistan, and Canada. These agreements enable India to quickly acquire the necessary uranium to meet the fuel requirements of its nuclear reactors under IAEA safeguards.

x: In India, some nuclear reactors kept under International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards while others are not as some use imported uranium and others use domestic supplies. s: Isotope 6C14 is associated with :
o: Determining the age of the earth
x: Radioisotope Carbon-14 (6C14) is used to determine the age of wood and bones (the time which elapsed after the death of plant or animal fossil) which is called Radiocarbon Dating. This technique is based on the decay of the Carbon-14 isotope in dead organism. The half–life of Carbon-14 is 5,730 + 40 years.

s: Carbon dating is used to determine the age of –
x: Carbon-14 dating is used for once-living organic remains such as fossils, wood and bones. It is not suited to dating rocks, which need uranium-lead or potassium-argon methods.

s: Which of the following technique is not relevant for dating of soil, minerals, rocks etc?
x: Radiocarbon, uranium-lead and potassium-argon are all radiometric dating methods. Mining is just extraction of minerals and not a dating technique.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radiometric dating?
o: Carbon-14 dating is used mainly for volcanic rocks older than a billion years
U-238 to Pb-206 dating is used for the oldest rocks and the age of the Earth
K-40 to Ar-40 dating is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers
Carbon-14 dating covers once-living remains up to about 50,000 years
x: Carbon-14 (half-life about 5,730 years) dates once-living organic remains up to about 50,000 years, not ancient volcanic rocks.

s: Which dating method is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers?
x: Potassium-argon dating suits volcanic rocks; Carbon-14 dates only once-living remains.

s: What is the half-life of Carbon-14?
x: C-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years; 50,000 years is the upper limit of what it can date.

s: Who pioneered uranium-lead dating, used to find the age of the Earth?
x: Clair Cameron Patterson pioneered uranium-lead dating; Stadler is known for induced mutation.

s: Up to how many years can Carbon-14 dating date once-living remains?
x: C-14 dates fossils, wood and bones up to about 50,000 years.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: What is the principle behind thermocouple?
Which one of the following is a spacecraft?
On which effect is the conversion of decay heat into electricity by thermocouples in a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) based?
x: An RTG is not a fission reactor; its thermocouples turn decay heat directly into electricity by the Seebeck effect, so it has no moving parts.

s: Which isotope is generally used as fuel in radioisotope thermoelectric generators?
x: Plutonium-238 is the fuel commonly associated with RTGs. It has been described as a by-product of weapons-development programmes.

s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of spacecraft or planetary missions associated with the use of RTG power sources?
x: Voyager, Cassini and Curiosity are examples of missions using RTG power where sunlight is weak. Perseverance is another such example.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs)?
o: An RTG uses Plutonium-238 as fuel
An RTG has no moving parts
An RTG is a type of fission reactor
x: An RTG is not a fission reactor; it turns decay heat of Pu-238 into electricity.

s: The RTG fuel Plutonium-238 is obtained as a by-product of what?
x: Pu-238, not Pu-239, is the RTG fuel and is a by-product of weapons production.

s:
Consider the following statements about food irradiation:
1. It works by radiolysis of water in the food.
2. Only Cobalt-60 gamma rays can be used as its source.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: food irradiation works by radiolysis of water. Statement 2 is wrong: the sources can be gamma rays (Co-60), X-rays or electron beams. So (b), (c) and (d) are wrong.

s: Who first demonstrated induced mutation in crop plants (barley) using X-rays?
x: L. J. Stadler first induced mutation in crop plants in 1928, using X-rays on barley. Gamma and neutron radiation were used later for mutation breeding.

s: TBM-9, a newer BARC Trombay variety developed with NRCB, Trichy, is a variety of which crop?
x: TBM-9 is the newer banana variety developed with NRCB, Trichy; RTS-43 is a sorghum variety.

s: In the sterile insect technique, radiation-sterilised males are released so that:
o: Mating with wild females produces no viable offspring
x: Gamma-sterilised males mate with wild females without producing viable offspring, so pest numbers decline.

s: What does the 'Radura' logo, an international symbol, indicate?
x: Radura is the international green symbol marking irradiated food. Organic, GM and fortified foods carry their own separate labels; Radura says only that the food was treated with radiation.

s: How many crop varieties have been developed using Trombay (BARC) technology?
x: 72 crop varieties have been developed by Trombay (BARC), a non-power use of nuclear technology that supports food security.

s: What are nuclear moisture gauges used to determine in agriculture?
x: Nuclear moisture gauges measure soil moisture and so help determine irrigation requirements.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about food irradiation in India?
o: Irradiation cannot be applied to bulk food
Irradiated mangoes have been exported to the United States
Irradiation can be carried out on packed food
x: Irradiation can be carried out on packed or bulk food.

s: RTS-43, a BARC Trombay variety, is a variety of which crop?
x: RTS-43 is a sorghum variety; TBM-9 is a banana variety.

s: Which radioisotope is used as a tracer to study fertiliser phosphorus uptake by plants?
x: P-32 is a fertiliser tracer for plant phosphorus uptake, besides its use in leukaemia.

s:
Consider the following statements about food irradiation:
1. It can use Cobalt-60 gamma rays, X-rays or electron beams.
2. It is the technique used to raise the genetic variety of crops.
3. It stops sprouting and kills pests.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Food irradiation uses Co-60 gamma, X-rays or electron beams to stop sprouting and kill pests; raising crop genetic variety is mutation breeding.

s: What is raising the genetic variety of crops by exposing them to radiation called?
x: Mutation breeding uses X-rays, gamma or neutron radiation to create new crop varieties.

s: Which of the following measures is suggested for flood mitigation?
Which of the following is NOT correct about industrial uses of radiotracers?
o: They detect leaks in buried oil and gas pipelines
Sediment tracking at ports increases the frequency of desilting campaigns
They are used to study seepage from dams
They are used for flow measurement
x: Radiotracer tracking of sediment transport can help reduce, not increase, the frequency of desilting campaigns.

s: Which alpha emitter is commonly used in smoke detectors?
x: Smoke detectors use an alpha emitter, commonly Americium-241. The other listed isotopes are associated with RTGs or industrial and medical radiation applications.

s: In industry, Sodium-24 is used as a tracer to detect what?
x: Na-24 detects pipeline leaks; weld radiography uses Ir-192 or Co-60 and smoke detectors use Am-241.

s: Gamma rays from which radioisotope are commonly used for radiation sterilisation of medical products?
x: Co-60 gamma rays are used for sterilisation as well as cancer radiotherapy.

s: How do radiotracers that track sediment movement help at ports?
x: Radiotracer sediment tracking at ports cuts how often desilting is needed.

s: Which of the following fruits is expected to be wiped out from the world as per the recent findings because of its narrow genetic base?
Which one of the following is NOT a stated effect or use of food irradiation?
o: Increasing the genetic diversity of crop seeds in the field
x: Food irradiation can stop sprouting, delay ripening and kill insects, parasites and pathogens. Increasing genetic diversity of field crops is associated with mutation breeding, not food irradiation.

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: What is the name of the instrument used to record and measure ionizing radiation in human beings?
x: A dosimeter records the dose of ionising radiation received by a person; a Geiger counter detects and counts radiation but does not measure the personal dose, and a radiometer measures radiant flux.
